'''''Erica ciliaris''''', the '''dorset heath''', is a species of flowering plant in the genus [[Erica (plant)|Erica]].<ref name="Stace">{{cite book|author=Clive A. Stace|author-link=Clive A. Stace|year=2010 |title=New Flora of the British Isles|edition=3rd|chapter=''Erica'' L. – heaths |pages=528–530|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=978-0-521-70772-5}}</ref>

== Description ==
It grows to {{convert|60|cm|abbr=off}}, and has leaves {{convert|2|-|4|mm|frac=16|2}} long, with long, glandular hairs.<ref name="Stace" /> The flowers are {{convert|8|-|12|mm|abbr=on|frac=8}} long, bright pink, and arranged in long [[raceme]]s.<ref name="Stace" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Erica ciliaris'' has a [[Lusitanian distribution]], stretching from Morocco in the south, along the Atlantic coasts of Portugal, Spain and France to south-western parts of the British Isles in the north.<ref>{{cite journal |author=S. B. Chapman|year=1975|title=The distribution and composition of hybrid populations of ''Erica ciliaris'' L. and ''Erica tetralix'' L. in Dorset|journal=[[Journal of Ecology]]|volume=63|issue=3|pages=809–823|doi=10.2307/2258603|jstor=2258603}}</ref> In the British Isles, it is only found natively in [[Dorset]], [[Devon]], [[Cornwall]] and one location in County Galway,<ref>Erica Ciliaris L. R. J. Rose, P. Bannister and S. B. Chapman Journal of Ecology Vol. 84, No. 4 (Aug., 1996), pp. 617–628</ref> where it lives in [[bog]]s and [[wet heath]]s.<ref name="Dorset">{{cite web|publisher=[[Plantlife]]|url=http://www.plantlife.org.uk/wild_plants/plant_species/dorset_heath/|work=County Flowers|title=Dorset heath ''(Erica ciliaris)''|accessdate=July 28, 2011|archive-date=21 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110921021759/http://www.plantlife.org.uk/wild_plants/plant_species/dorset_heath|url-status=dead}}</ref> It has also been [[introduced species|introduced]] to [[Hampshire]].<ref name="Stace" />

== In culture ==
''E. ciliaris'' was voted the [[County flowers of the United Kingdom|county flower]] of Dorset in 2002 following a poll by the wild flora conservation charity [[Plantlife]].<ref name="Dorset" />
